title: Countable-colimit preserving full embeddings have retract-closed image
statement: Use universes, quasicategories, coherent functors, full subcategories, mapping spaces, homotopies, equivalences and colimits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A countable simplicial set means one having at most countably many nondegenerate simplices, including the empty set. Let $i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a fully faithful coherent functor of infinity categories in a fixed universe. Suppose $\mathcal C$ admits colimits of every coherent diagram indexed by a countable simplicial set and $i$ preserves these colimits. Then the essential image of $i$ is closed under homotopy retracts: if $c\in\mathcal C$, $x\in\mathcal D$, and there are arrows $a:x\to i(c)$ and $b:i(c)\to x$ with a homotopy $ba\simeq1_x$, then there is $c\prime\in\mathcal C$ and an equivalence $i(c\prime)\simeq x$. The essential image consists of objects equivalent to some $i(c)$; neither presentability nor accessibility is assumed.

source.place: HTT Corollary 4.4.5.7 (a weak retraction extends coherently), Proposition 4.4.5.12, Corollaries 4.4.5.14–4.4.5.16 and Remark 4.4.5.18, printed pp. 305–308. A retraction is a colimit of a countable walking-idempotent diagram; full embeddings preserving those colimits preserve its splitting. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Let $R$ be the explicitly described two-object retraction category in [lem-coef-weak-retraction-coherent-extension], and let $I=N(R|_{\{X\}})$. Thus $I$ is the nerve of the one-object category with endomorphisms $1,e$ and $e^2=e$. By the nerve definition [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], an $n$-simplex is a string of $n$ endomorphisms. Any string containing $1$ is a degeneracy, obtained by inserting that identity, and every degeneracy contains an identity. Hence the only nondegenerate $n$-simplex is the string of $n$ copies of $e$; for $n=0$ it is the unique vertex. There is exactly one nondegenerate simplex in every degree, so $I$ is countable in the precise sense of the hypothesis. All these sets lie in the fixed universe.

source.place: Definition 4.4.5.2 and Remark 4.4.5.3, printed p.304; elementary count of strings in the nerve.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-weak-retraction-coherent-extension] with $\mathcal E=\mathcal D$, $u=i(c)$, $v=x$ and the given arrows $a,b$ and homotopy $ba\simeq1_x$. It supplies $F:N(R)\to\mathcal D$ with those same objects and arrows, retaining a weak-retraction triangle. Put $H=F|_I$. The cocone $\lambda_F:H\to\Delta_I x$ of [lem-coef-strong-retraction-idem-colimit] is colimiting in $\mathcal D$. This supplies all the coherences of $H$ and its cocone; an equation for the component of $ab$ in a homotopy category alone is not substituted for that data.

Let $\mathcal D_0$ be the full replete essential image of $i$. Since the only vertex of $H$ is $i(c)$, every simplex of $H$ has its vertices in $\mathcal D_0$, so $H$ factors as $H_0:I\to\mathcal D_0$ by the full-subcategory definition. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to the given fully faithful $i$; with $i_0:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D_0$ it supplies a coherent inverse $K:\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal C$ and $i_0K\simeq1_{\mathcal D_0}$. Set $G=KH_0$. Restrict the latter natural equivalence along $H_0$ and then include into $\mathcal D$ to obtain a coherent equivalence $\epsilon:iG\simeq H$. The inverse and its two triangle witnesses restrict and include too. Thus the entire coherent diagram lifts, without choosing independent lifts of its simplices.

source.place: The full-essential-image lifting argument applied to HTT Section 4.4.5; agent expansion using the existing coherent quasi-inverse theorem.

proof.text: By Step 1 the shape $I$ is countable. Apply the assumed existence of countable colimits in $\mathcal C$ to $G$, and choose a colimiting cocone $\mu:G\to\Delta_I c\prime$. The assumed preservation by $i$ makes $\bar\mu=i\mu:iG\to\Delta_I i(c\prime)$ a colimiting cocone in $\mathcal D$. Only this particular countable colimit is used. This is an application of the two explicit hypotheses, using the definition of colimiting cocone; no cocompleteness of $\mathcal D$ is invoked.

source.place: Corollaries 4.4.5.14-4.4.5.15, printed p.308; direct application of the item hypotheses to the countable shape I.

proof.text: Write $T=\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal D)$, which is a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Choose the inverse equivalence $\epsilon^{-1}:H\to iG$, and form $\nu=\bar\mu\circ\epsilon^{-1}:H\to\Delta_I i(c\prime)$ using composition in $T$. For every $z\in\mathcal D$ the universal map for this cocone factors, up to the canonical associativity homotopy, as $$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(i(c\prime),z)\xrightarrow{\bar\mu^*}\operatorname{Map}_T(iG,\Delta_I z)\xrightarrow{(\epsilon^{-1})^*}\operatorname{Map}_T(H,\Delta_I z).$$ The first map is an equivalence by the dual universal mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] and Step 4. The second has homotopy inverse $\epsilon^*$: for any $q$, the two composites are $q\circ(\epsilon\circ\epsilon^{-1})\simeq q$ and $q\circ(\epsilon^{-1}\circ\epsilon)\simeq q$, using the inverse triangles, associativity, units and component dependence of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], now applied in $T$. Its mapping spaces are Kan by the cone calculus, and [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] turns these simplicial homotopy inverses into weak equivalences. The composite is therefore an equivalence of spaces. Applying the same dual criterion again proves that $\nu$ is colimiting. This writes out the comparison along $\epsilon$ rather than silently identifying equivalent diagrams.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.12 and Corollary 4.4.5.14, printed pp.307-308; agent expansion of invariance under the coherent equivalence of the lifted diagram, using the cited mapping-space criteria.

proof.text: The cocones $\lambda_F$ of Step 2 and $\nu$ of Step 5 are initial objects of the same coherent cocone quasicategory on $H$. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], its full subcategory of initial objects is a contractible Kan complex, so these two cocones are equivalent. Project this equivalence and its inverse-triangle witnesses to their apices, using the degreewise cocone projection of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. It gives an equivalence $i(c\prime)\simeq x$ in $\mathcal D$, as required. No property of the initial choice of $c$ beyond its membership in $\mathcal C$ was used.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.12, printed p.307, and uniqueness of colimits; explicit use of the existing initial-object contractibility theorem.

proof_origin.place: HTT Section 4.4.5, especially Definition 4.4.5.2, Remark 4.4.5.3, Corollary 4.4.5.7 and Proposition 4.4.5.12, printed pp.303-308, read online. Agent expansion through the existing full-essential-image and coherent comma mapping-space calculus; local archive WANTED.
